rows.synopsis: On her sixteenth birthday, Eva leaves the only home she has ever known to find the family she has always dreamed about.
rows.situation: Eva grew up alone in Sanctuary 573, raised by the robot Muthr and counting down to the Final Assessment that will let her join other humans on the surface. Training done, she sneaks into a restricted room and finds empty pods with names on them, other kids who were supposed to be there, and a voice in the dark, Wondla, find me, before something in the dark attacks.
rows.coping: When the intruder breaches the sanctuary, Muthr makes the choice she has been protecting Eva for: she sends her up the vent shaft to the surface with supplies and stays behind, and Eva steps onto a surface nothing in her training prepared her for, carrying the question of whether anyone is out there looking for her.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis gives the leaving; the script carries the childhood flashback (Meego, Cadmus Pryde hologram, Muthr's we are not a family line), the sixteen-year test-day nerves, the empty pod room, the Wondla message, and the attack that forces the escape. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva's whole life has been Sanctuary 573: Muthr the multi-utility task helper robot, Meego the playmate hologram, and a sixteen-year wait for the Final Assessment that will open the big door to other humans. On test day she cannot wait, sneaks into a restricted room, and finds the pods meant for six children in her generation, all empty, all with names, and a voice asking Eva to find Wondla. Then something unknown attacks, the sanctuary locks down, and Muthr, programmed to keep her safe, stays behind to hold it off and sends Eva up the vent shaft alone. The surface she emerges onto is not the world her training vids promised.

rows.synopsis: Eva meets her first aliens on the surface, evades a monster hunter named Besteel, and discovers she's not on the world she expected.
rows.situation: Eva's survival training meets reality: walking trees, flying whales, and a giant butterfly are all missing from Omni's database, and a hunter called Besteel snatches Omni before Eva escapes with help from a green forest spirit she names Shee-nah. A waterbear named Otto glides them to safety, speaks to Eva in her head, and a chewy jargum pellet lets everyone understand each other, just in time for Besteel to catch up.
rows.coping: Eva leans on exactly what she trained for, provisions, first-aid on Muthr's circuit board with sticky sap, and a deal-making streak: she bargains the Omnipod itself to the grumpy stranger for passage to Lacus, where her one real clue, a Dynastes patch, came from. The stranger's name, she finally learns, is Rovender Kitt.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names Besteel; the script carries the database-gaps comedy, the Shee-nah rescue and jargum understanding, Otto's telepathy, the Omni-as-collateral deal, and Muthr's reveal that Eva's sanctuary was contaminated and Eva was the only pod that survived. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva's first day on the surface breaks every rule in her training: trees walk, whales fly, and Omni's database comes up empty again and again. She is stolen from, rescued by a spiky green spirit she insists on calling Shee-nah, and saved from the hunter Besteel by Otto, a waterbear who hears her thoughts. A shared jargum pellet unlocks real communication, and Eva seals the deal: the grumpy stranger gets the Omnipod to trade in Lacus, and Eva gets a guide to the place her Dynastes patch came from, proof other humans existed. Then Muthr's systems come back online with a harder truth: this world has rings, and it might not be the Earth Eva was raised for.

rows.synopsis: Eva reaches the bustling town of Lacus, where a race bet, a junk-shop clue, and a family dinner all push her search for other humans forward.
rows.situation: On the road to Lacus Eva rescues a baby sand sniper against everyone's advice, costing them time and nearly them all to Besteel. In Lacus, the antique dealer Caruncle will sell the patch's origin story for 300 shellacks, so Eva bets Omni at the spiderfish races, and the family she is looking for starts arriving in a different form: Rovender's sister Fiscian's dinner table.
rows.coping: Eva's compassion is tested and costs her: the baby sand sniper she tries to save is snatched by Besteel anyway, and she has to carry that loss forward. At Fiscian's, ten-toe questions and pentaka lessons show Eva what family dinner feels like, and Fiscian's story of how Rovender lost his own family reframes the grumpiest member of her found family.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis follows the town day; the script carries the sand-sniper rescue and Besteel trap, Caruncle's 300-shellack price, the race wager of the Omnipod itself, the dinner scene and ten-toes questions, and the Zoozi/Darius mystery and Arsian sage foreshadowing. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva hears a baby sand sniper crying for its mother when no one else can, and her compassion nearly gets everyone killed when Besteel's trap and the hunter himself arrive; she learns that saving someone is not always the same as saving them. In Lacus, Caruncle's palace of junk holds the origin of the Dynastes patch, for 300 shellacks, so Eva bets Omni at the spiderfish races and gets a lesson in luck. Rovender's sister Fiscian serves pentaka and ten-toes questions, and her glimpse of Rovender almost happy for the first time in years shows Eva what her found family is becoming. The chapter closes with Eva turning Omni's location tracking off and a sage upstairs who dreams about humans.

rows.synopsis: Eva visits the mysterious Darius hoping to learn what happened to the humans, and the answer she gets is not the one she wanted.
rows.situation: Darius trades memories for memories and shows Eva her own happy sixth-birthday belief that humans waited for her on the surface, then gifts her the planet's past: humans destroyed the old world and buried themselves with it, and to Darius even one more human underground is too many. Eva runs, Otto saves her from drowning, and the question becomes unbearable, what if she is the only one.
rows.coping: Eva finds the strength to keep going through the found family she has built: Otto tells her she is not alone, the Dynastes patch proves another sanctuary-born existed, and a lead emerges, Caruncle sold an Omnipod to someone named Zin in Solas. Rovender, told he is nothing but a washed-up drifter, walks away drunk, leaving Eva to face Besteel alone.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the sage visit; the script carries the memory-for-memory gift exchange, the humans-destroyed-the-planet revelation, Rovender's relapse and split over the winnings, the Muthr argument that ends in you are not my real mother, and Besteel capturing Eva at the bar. confidence high. vibe corrected to the ratified lowercase set (was sad, which is an emotion, not a felt energy).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva climbs to the house where Darius the Arsian sage lives, and the price of answers is a memory: Darius replays Eva's own sixth-birthday certainty that family waited on the surface, then gives her the truth in return, humans wrecked the world and buried themselves with it, and Darius casts Eva out as a monster for being human. Otto fishes her out of despair, and the Dynastes patch plus a new lead, an Omnipod sold to Zin in Solas, give her a reason to keep moving. Rovender, called a washed-up drifter, quits the deal, Muthr and Eva trade the words that hurt most, you are not my real mother, and Besteel walks into the bar and takes Eva.

rows.synopsis: Captured and delivered to Queen Ojo's court in Solas, Eva makes an unlikely friend and plans her escape.
rows.situation: Besteel presents Eva to the court as a living human specimen, and court scientist Loroc looks forward to studying and dissecting her. Eva escapes the guards with help from Zin, Queen Ojo's own daughter, who sneaks her into her late father's sealed collection of human artifacts, where the two lonely girls hunt the Omnipod and play a pinball machine together.
rows.coping: Eva works the escape with nerve and new friendship: she bluffs brain-melting powers, and the sand-sniper demonstration she stages convinces Zin to side with her against Loroc's threats. Zin stands up to Loroc with her father's scepter at stake, hands Eva the coordinates from the Omni she kept, and accepts being removed from her own throne to see Eva free.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis gives the capture and escape; the script carries the Loroc dissection threat, the brain-melt bluff, King Ojo's human-artifact collection and Chip the guardian, the pinball first-friendship scene, Zin's dethroning, and the Omni's coordinates pointing 159.25 miles to the original owner. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Besteel delivers Eva to Queen Ojo's court, where Brother Loroc calls her a dangerous, mercurial race and schedules a dissection. The escape comes from the unlikeliest ally: Zin, the queen's daughter and a girl who has never had a friend either, hides Eva in her father's sealed collection of human artifacts, where the two play a pinball machine, nail their first high five, and admit they each grew up alone. When Loroc moves to cage Zin herself, she hands over the scepter's truth and the Omni's coordinates, 159.25 miles to the original owner, and Eva flees Solas with two stolen Omnipods, a queen dethroned on her behalf, and a direction to run.

rows.synopsis: Reunited with Muthr, Eva leads her found family across a collapsing sulfur bridge toward a possible human civilization.
rows.situation: Muthr is found damaged by desert grit, Rovender returns warning that Besteel is tracking them, and the last approach to the human city crosses a corroded bridge over sulfuric acid. The Goldfish is lost, the pathway is incomplete, and Eva insists on the impossible plan: Otto plus balance plus a ramp made of speed.
rows.coping: Eva learns to accept trust instead of doing it all alone: Rovender shares the rope he made from his lost family's clothes and says she gave him his path back, and Otto glides everyone to safety. Eva apologizes to Muthr for calling her just a robot, and the crew walks out onto Wondla, the human city real at last.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis gives the mission; the script carries the Muthr reunion, the Rovender return and bridge guidance, the Otto jump and Goldfish loss, the family-clothes rope speech, the just-a-robot apology, and the Wondla reveal. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The chapter opens with reunion: Muthr battered but back, Rovender returned because Eva believed in him when he could not believe in himself, and a clue in hand, coordinates to other humans. The price of getting there is a corroded bridge over sulfuric acid, a lost Goldfish, and Eva's own reckless plan that nearly kills Otto. At the lowest point, Eva owns every hurt word she said in Lacus, and Rovender, carrying a rope made from his lost family's clothes, tells her she is not letting her hope go. Otto glides the whole family across, and the city lights they find are not a promise anymore, they are Wondla.

rows.synopsis: Eva reaches the ruins of a human city and finds the last thing she expected, and loses the one she loves most.
rows.situation: Beacons lead Eva through the ruins of a city that held 8.38 million people to an operational Omnipod signal, and the voice she finds is Roshon's recording: the sanctuaries all failed, what we were promised was all a lie. Besteel, sent by Loroc to finish the job, hunts Eva into the New York Public Library while Muthr and Otto work to free themselves.
rows.coping: Eva faces the question of why she was brought to a wasteland, and Muthr answers it with the truth that redefines family: she chose to be Eva's mother because she loves her. After Muthr is destroyed shielding her, Eva calls for help and Otto comes, and Rovender tells her Muthr's loving spirit lives within her now, before a familiar airship arrives, Cadmus Pryde, here to take her home.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis understates the gut-punch; the script carries the beacon trail, Roshon's the-sanctuaries-failed recording, the Besteel library hunt and who-is-the-monster confrontation, Muthr's destruction and final choice-to-be-your-mother words, and the Cadmus Pryde airship cliffhanger. confidence high. vibe corrected to the ratified lowercase set (was sad, which is an emotion, not a felt energy).
rows.per_story_synopsis: The beacons lead Eva to a city built for millions and a single operating Omnipod whose owner, Roshon, left a recording: every sanctuary failed, everything they were promised was a lie. Alone in the ruins, Eva is hunted by Besteel, sent by Loroc to take the last human skull, until Muthr throws herself between them and does not survive it. Her final words give Eva what no training ever did, I made a choice to be your mother because I love you, and Otto answers the call for help when it matters. The season closes on an airship descending with a voice Eva has known all her life: greetings, Eva, I am Cadmus Pryde, and I am here to take you home.

rows.synopsis: Eva arrives in the human city of New Attica, meets the real Cadmus Pryde, and finds her welcome is not quite what it seems.
rows.situation: Cadmus's retrieval hologram leads Eva to a pilot, Hailey van Turner, whose flying Bijou carries her over the valley to a city of 2.2 million humans. Rovender and Otto say goodbye at the gates because aliens cannot enter, Cadmus greets her in person, and after a first day of games with new friends Gen and Nova, the Muthr waiting in her living unit is not her Muthr at all, and a girl who looks just like her is watching.
rows.coping: Eva lets herself enjoy the arrival, games, new friends, a city built for her, and thanks the friends who walked her home. But she trusts her own senses when the replacement Muthr starts uploading unfamiliar settings, asks Omni to dim the lights, and discovers a second Eva hiding in the shadows of her new home.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis gives the arrival; the script carries Hailey and the Bijou, the farewell at the gates, the Meego tour and real Cadmus, the Jolt game with the water-beast punch, the fake Muthr reveal, and the lookalike-Eva ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The airship brings Eva not to her parents but to New Attica, Cadmus Pryde's protected city of 2.2 million humans, and the real Cadmus is warm, apologetic, and proud. Rovender and Otto part from her at the gates because her Wondla is not theirs, and Eva's first day delivers everything the sanctuaries promised: friends, games, sunshine, a home. Then the Muthr in her living unit calls itself Unit 248 and begins uploading strange settings, and in the dark Eva finds the last thing New Attica should contain: another girl with her face, waiting.

rows.synopsis: Eva chases a mysterious Sanctuary jacket through New Attica and discovers a sister she never knew she had.
rows.situation: Eva spots a real sanctuary jacket among the New Atticans, and the chase ends in a hidden sanctuary where Eva 8 of Sanctuary 573, raised sixteen years before Eva by the same Muthr, has been surviving with outsiders Kai, Xander, and Violet. Eight's sanctlings all died on the surface, and it was Eva's reset sanctuary that refused her reentry, a grief she has carried into a distrust of Cadmus.
rows.coping: The sisters trade the stories that broke them: Eight's the-sanctuaries-failed grief and Eva's loss of Muthr, and Eight offers to take care of her, we are sisters. But the reunion is short-lived, Eva's escort Omni tracks her to the unsanctioned location, and Cadmus greets Eva 8 with a gazpacho welcome and a look that knows more than it says.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names the discovery; the script carries the gondola chase, the hidden-sanctuary outsiders, Eight's sanctlings backstory and denied reentry, the tracker deactivation, and Cadmus's knowing welcome. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: A sanctuary jacket in a crowd of New Atticans sends Eva on a chase that ends in the family she never knew: Eva 8, raised in the same Sanctuary 573 a generation earlier, sole survivor of sanctlings who died when the surface failed them, turned away by her own home when the cycle reset for Eva 9. The sisters' reunion is tender and haunted, Eight's guilt met by Eva's insistence that none of it was her fault. But Eva's Omni betrays the hiding place, Cadmus arrives with gazpacho and questions, and Otto's warning lands hard, the nice man is not nice.

rows.synopsis: Desperate to locate her captured friends, Eva breaks into Cadmus's lab and learns why New Attica really needs her.
rows.situation: Cadmus traps Rovender and Otto underground, and Eva and Eight follow tunnel maps to a lab holding Otto in a hostile machine body and a dying Rovender. A leaked board meeting reveals New Attica has one month of food left, its vertical farms are dying, and Cadmus plans to use alien life and Eva's unique ability to renew the planet.
rows.coping: Eva refuses to leave her friends, hiding from the Authoriton patrol units while trying to reach the holding cells, and commits to getting the injured Rovender home to Faunas. Eight and the outsiders scatter to Trievertown with what they salvaged, and the rescue becomes a mission: get out of New Attica, get Rovender help, expose Cadmus.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names the rescue; the script carries the Omni escort trick, the dead vertical farms and thermal vent, Otto's machine body, Rovender's injury, the board-meeting one-month-of-food reveal, and Vanpa's capture covering the escape. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The search for Rovender and Otto takes Eva and Eight through New Attica's underground, past dead vertical farms and a thermal vent that powers the city, into Cadmus's lab, where Otto wakes in a hostile metal body and Rovender lies dying with one request, get me home to Faunas. The overheard board meeting explains everything: one month of food, a dying biome, Authoritons to control unrest, and Cadmus studying alien life to save the colony. The escape costs Vanpa his freedom, Hailey fires up the Bijou for the Green Spot, and Eva leaves the city of her dreams carrying her hurt family and the beginnings of the truth.

rows.synopsis: After a warbot attack forces the Bijou down, Eva, Eight, and Hailey carry the injured Rovender across the wastelands toward Faunas.
rows.situation: Cadmus's flying warbots shoot the Bijou out of the sky, and the group survives the crash only to face the black winds, the hunting ground of the Dawosu, with Rovender's condition failing. Eight's grief surfaces in the open: she lost her sister Freya to the Dawosu, and history looks ready to repeat itself.
rows.coping: Eva tries to reason with the monster and it nearly costs everything, Rovender offering himself as bait so the rest can move on. She refuses to leave him, and the truth she learns is hard and useful: some things cannot be reasoned with, the Dawosu was only protecting its nest, and some dangers you survive by avoiding, not befriending.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the crash and trek; the script carries Hailey's best-glide emergency landing, the wandering tree and Mirthian water-straw ambush, Boodoo Obeedo's spiderfish-race connection, the black-winds warning, Eight's Freya loss, Rovender's sacrifice attempt, and the Dawosu nest revelation. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The skies are not safe either: warbots force the Bijou into a crash landing, and the walk to Faunas crosses the hunting ground of the Dawosu, the creature Eight's sister died to. Hailey's flying skill, the Mirthians' water and directions, and a spiderfish racing secret from Lacus all help, but the monster comes anyway, and Rovender walks out to give himself to it. Eva's gift for talking to creatures meets its limit here, the Dawosu protecting its nest is not a creature to be reasoned with, and the lesson lands with her sister's grief beside her. They make it to the Green Spot, with Faunas in sight and Rovender still fighting.

rows.synopsis: Eva brings a dying Rovender home to Faunas, only to find his village has branded him a deserter, and she challenges the charge before the whole community.
rows.situation: Faunas refuses Rovender entry and his father, Antiquus, calls him a traitor with no honor. Eva risks the walls at night to steal the kasavi he needs, is caught, and her challenge of the elder's word triggers a Kawona trial: she must find the Bird of Revelation and offer it a truth from deep in her heart.
rows.coping: Eva's truth is simple and complete: Rovender saved her in big and small ways, he is her family, he is her father, and that is what fathers do. The trial forces Antiquus to see the same, and the truth that was in front of everyone all along, a father's love should be unconditional, becomes the plea that saves his son.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis gives the trial; the script carries the gate refusal, the kasavi theft and Gargoof comedy, the deserter accusation, the Kawona quest on a whale, Rovender's own confession about losing Hanno and Gisana, and Eva's save-my-son truth. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Homecoming goes wrong: the village that will not help a human is Rovender's own, his father is its elder, and the charge against him is desertion. Eva answers with action first, sneaking in for the medicine, then with the boldest move she has made, challenging Antiquus in front of everyone and earning a trial that can only be won with the Kawona, a bird that comes only when offered a true thing from the heart. Rovender confesses his own truth first, the day he lost his wife and daughter and could not bear to stay. Eva's truth follows, that the man they call deserter is her father in every way that counts, and the truth standing in front of them all is a father's unconditional love.

rows.synopsis: At the Joyous Bloom celebration, Eva connects with the Heart of the Forest, and Cadmus's warbots descend on Faunas to take it.
rows.situation: The village celebrates the Heart of the Forest, Eva receives a jargum and hears every creature speak, and during the ceremony she has a vision of the Heart's origin as the life bringer that seeded Orbona. Then Cadmus's warbots breach the celebration, and Eva realizes he has been using her connection to lead him to the Heart, with Hailey's tracker as his map.
rows.coping: Faunas refuses to abandon its kin, and the evacuation becomes a stand: Otto's hiding trick saves the village, the tar fields trap the metal walkers, and Teal the munt-runner gives everything in the fight. Eva tries to lead Cadmus away to protect everyone, and the parting twist lands hard, Hailey was tracking them for Vanpa's sake, and Cadmus takes Eva anyway, calling her the only human left who can save the human race.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis gives the celebration and attack; the script carries the jargum gift and creature-hearing, Eight's departure to Trievertown, the Heart vision in Muthr's voice, the evacuation and Otto's hiding trick, the sticky-mud plan, Teal's fall, Hailey's leg, the Hailey-was-tracking reveal, and Cadmus taking Eva. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Joyous Bloom gives Eva everything found family can offer, a home, a language for the creatures she loves, a village celebration, and even Eight, before Eight chooses her own path to Trievertown. Then the vision comes in Muthr's voice, the Heart of the Forest launched long ago to bring a dead planet to life, and Eva understands why Cadmus wanted her so badly. The warbot assault that follows is answered by the whole village, Otto's hiding trick, sticky mud, and Teal's sacrifice, but Cadmus wins the day through Hailey's tracker, a betrayal made for the noblest reason, Vanpa's life. The episode closes with Cadmus holding Eva, the one human he believes can save the human race, and Eight demanding he let her sister go.

rows.synopsis: Cadmus uses Eva as a compass to hunt the Heart of the Forest, and what she finds there is not an energy source but a consciousness, wearing the face of her mother.
rows.situation: Strapped to Cadmus's machine, Eva's fear feeds the connection to the source as he closes in. Refusing to lead him to the Heart, she risks her own failing body to warn it, reaches the sanctuary, and meets the Heart itself, which appears to her as Muthr. It answers the coming humans with one idea: there is no them, only us.
rows.coping: Eva stays calm under fear, protects the creatures others would call them, and tries to warn the Heart even while critically injured. The Heart reassures her the way a mother would, do not fear, my child, but when Eva reaches out to Eight she collapses, and the season ends on grief and an open question, whether the Heart's oneness can survive a species that divides the world into us and them.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis gives the hunt; the script carries the compass machine and sympathetic fear response, Cadmus's eat-or-be-eaten speech, the injured warning run, the Heart-as-Muthr revelation with I have many names, the no-them-only-us refrain, Eva's collapse, and the sorry-I-was-supposed-to-protect-you ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Cadmus straps Eva to his machine and turns her part-alien connection into a compass, her fear literally strengthening the signal as they close on the source. She holds herself calm, refuses to be a weapon, and bleeds her way to the sanctuary to warn the Heart before he arrives. What waits there has taken Muthr's shape, the Heart of the Forest, an unbounded consciousness with many names, and it greets the threat of human violence with a terrifying tenderness: there is no them, only us. Eva, unable to make it understand that the humans will kill it, collapses into Eight's arms, and the season closes on the promise that the Heart, like every mother, will go on, and so will she.

rows.synopsis: Left for dead after Cadmus's machine, Eight wakes inside New Attica determined to expose him, and turns his own broadcast stage into her stage.
rows.situation: Eight recovers Vanpa and the outsider crew, hacks the mainframe, and stages an elaborate trap, Cat to Pest Control code names and all, to catch Cadmus in front of witnesses. Cadmus lets her think she is the player, then reveals he watched her every step and turns her capture into a forced atonement broadcast.
rows.coping: Eight refuses the role Cadmus writes for her: on live screens in front of all New Attica she confesses to nothing he scripted, shows the citizens the dying crops and the fake dome sky, and names New Attica a prison. Her truth, that Cadmus gave up on the world and she will not, lands as a call to action, even as Cadmus answers it with a darker one, he will kill every last alien.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the rebellion; the script carries the Eva-is-dead mourning and blame, the magnetic seal hack and Sanc-Bo raiders, the gondola trap sequence, Cadmus's you-are-the-pawn reversal and you-did-it blame, and the broadcast takeover ending. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Season 3 opens inside New Attica with grief turned into war: Eight, told Eva is dead and it is her fault, breaks back in with Vanpa's crew, hacks the city's mainframe, and catches Cadmus in a chase he claims to have scripted all along. Forced to atone on camera, Eight seizes the broadcast instead, showing the citizens the lies behind the dome sky and the truth of the world outside as their birthright. Cadmus's answer closes the trap of the season: he will harness the Source as a weapon and kill every last alien, and he still needs Eight to believe she has no alternative.

rows.synopsis: Eva wakes to a dying Orbona, meets the sage Arius, and returns to a Solas on the brink of civil war to find her allies, and herself, on trial.
rows.situation: Eva survives, reunites with Rovender and Otto, and follows Arius's lead to Queen Ojo in Solas, where Loroc is seizing power by blaming humans for the dying forest. Eva reveals herself to the court, is disbelieved and sentenced, and Zin helps her and the queen escape through a secret exit as Redimus and the loyalists hold the line.
rows.coping: Arius reframes Eva's failure as the future's flexibility, the future is never fixed, and gives her a first step instead of a verdict. Queen Ojo risks her throne to testify that Eva is her friend, and the escape plan is built on trust, the Heart must stay in its casing, and the mission is clear: get to New Attica before Loroc's army does.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the return; the script carries Arius's not-my-sister introduction and ninth-of-Evas naming, the Faunas reunion, the Gargoof-the-shaman disguise gambit, the court reveal, Loroc's coup, Zin's help, the Heart-casing warning, and the thermal-vent plan. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva wakes alone on a dying planet, saves a stranded creature, and finds Arius, Darius's identical sister, who sees all that could be and tells her the future is never fixed. The reunion with Rovender and Otto is brief and warm, and then Eva walks into Solas wearing the face of the enemy's scapegoat: Loroc is using the forest's death to seize his sister's throne. Eva's court reveal gambles everything and nearly loses it, until Zin chooses Orbona over his brother and the queen chooses her friend over her crown. The escape hands the season its quest, deliver the Heart to the thermal vent at the planet's core, with the warning hanging over everything, the Heart must always be in the casing.

rows.synopsis: To outrun Loroc's army, Eva and Queen Ojo risk occupied Lacus, face the viceroy who sold it out, and spark a city's rebellion.
rows.situation: A race against pillar guards brings the team to Lacus, where Caruncle has installed himself as viceroy, confiscating fish and heirlooms for Loroc's war and posting a kill-on-sight reward for Eva and the queen. In disguise, Eva and Redimus try to bargain for the Bijou, Redimus is captured, and Hostia shelters the fugitives.
rows.coping: Eva and her friends fight the occupation with nerve and humor, a fake royal-secret-service badge and a boomrod story that riles Caruncle, until the queen takes the boldest path: revealing herself to the city from the Bijou's hatch, calling her people out of the shadows into the light. The crowd cuts the ship loose, Redimus stays to stand with the queen, and a new Omnipod joins the family for the flight to New Attica.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names the race; the script carries Vanpa's jargum, the disguise and reward posters, Caruncle's giveaway and viceroy title comedy, Redimus's capture, Hostia's shelter, the queen's hatch speech, the crowd rescue, and the new Omnipod send-off. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Loroc's un-resting pillar guards force a do-or-die detour to Lacus for the Bijou, and the town Eva once visited for a race has fallen: Caruncle the viceroy taxes everything not nailed down, Otto swims in disguise, and a million-shellack bounty hangs over Eva and the queen. The heist for the ship goes sideways when Redimus buys time with his freedom, and Hostia's home becomes the refuge. The rescue is the queen's alone to make: she steps out over the city and asks her people to leave the shadows and fight for their families, and Lacus answers, cutting the Bijou free. The episode ends with Redimus and the queen staying to hold it, and Eva flying on with a chatty new Omnipod and a war to win.

rows.synopsis: Eva reunites with Eight at last, only to learn that Eight leads New Attica's assault on the aliens, and their reunion becomes a battle over who is the monster.
rows.situation: Eva lands near the geothermal vent with the plan set, but Eight, believing Eva died and blaming herself, has seized control of New Attica and orders Eva taken for deprogramming as infected by aliens. When the migrating creatures of Orbona arrive drawn to the Heart, Eight prepares to fire on them, and the sisters stand on opposite sides of the same war.
rows.coping: Eva refuses to fight her sister and instead calls to the herd the way she once talked to Otto, turning the creatures away from the Heart to safety. Rovender tells her never to give up trying to reach Eight, Otto chooses family and promises not goodbye, and Eva admits she does not know if she can restore the Heart, then goes anyway, leading a new band of allies to save Orbona.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names the reunion; the script carries the Eight-in-charge reveal and deprogramming order, the Fours resistance and Frank, the migrating herd, the mother-creature shooting and you-are-the-monster line, Eva's herd-turning, and the not-goodbye Otto farewell. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The reunion Eva crossed a planet for is the season's cruelest twist: Eight survived, leads New Attica now, and greets her sister with a deprogramming cell, convinced Eva has been infected by aliens. Eva's story of the Heart wearing Muthr's face changes nothing, and when Orbona's creatures come migrating home to the Heart, Eight orders weapons free and shoots down a mother. Eva answers with the only power she has, turning the whole herd away from danger with her voice, and walks out of Trievertown with Otto's not-goodbye, a ragtag crew, and a promise she is not sure she can keep: restore the Heart and save Orbona anyway.

rows.synopsis: Amid the fog of war, Eva searches New Attica for the Heart, and Cadmus reveals Eight has rigged Project Sunshine, a bomb meant to end every alien on Orbona.
rows.situation: Vanpa's repaired warbot smuggles Eva and Redimus into the besieged city, where Eight's forces and the alien army clash as civilians evacuate. The Heart is in Cadmus's office, but Cadmus, freed and chastened, confesses the real horror: Eight weaponized the Source into a bomb atop the pyramid and lured the herd in as a trap.
rows.coping: Eva takes Cadmus at his word and turns an enemy into an ally, if you are sorry, help me. Cadmus gives her the original Omni, universal access and the entire history of their people, and stays behind to face what he built, telling her what Muthr once told her, I will go on and so will you. Otto shields them one last time, saying not goodbye, and Eva presses on toward the thermal vent with Rovender refusing to leave her side.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis covers the search; the script carries Vanpa's warbot infiltration, Redimus's prisoner gambit, the evacuation and battle, the Meego runaway gondola comedy, Cadmus's Project Sunshine confession, the original Omni handoff, and Otto's sacrifice and survival. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The infiltration of New Attica is part heist, part comedy, and all stakes: Vanpa drives a patched-together warbot, Redimus volunteers as a prisoner, and a Meego-driven gondola nearly ends the quest with french-fry beams. The Heart is found, but so is the season's darkest truth, Eight has turned the Source into Project Sunshine, a bomb luring Orbona's own creatures to their deaths. Cadmus, the villain of two seasons, asks to help fix what he made, hands Eva the original Omni and the history of her people, and stays to hold the line. Otto's not-goodbye and survival carry Eva and Rovender toward the thermal vent with the Heart and almost no time.

rows.synopsis: With the fate of the planet at stake, Eva races to deliver the Heart to the thermal vent, and Eight must choose between the war she built and the family that never left her.
rows.situation: Loroc declares himself savior of the planet and blocks the way, Eight confronts Eva as one of them, and Rovender falls in the fighting. At the sealed tunnel, Eva's pleas seem answered only when the very creatures she saved come to her rescue, and Vanpa's Fours buy the last passage with everything they have.
rows.coping: Eva holds the line against becoming what the war wants: she gives Eight jargum so she can finally understand the creatures, and Rovender's last words, do not let this change you, echo Arius's. The Heart answers Eight's returning-home plea with there is no them, only us, Eva names herself the bridge and goes with the Heart, and the epilogue tells the whole arc plainly, a nymph who went in search of a family, a home, and the truth, and found them intertwined.
rows.notes: script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis compresses the finale; the script carries Loroc's savior claim and fraud takedown, Vanpa's magnet trap and Evan-4 sign-off, the Fours rescue, Rovender's fall and jargum plea, Eight's seeking-re-entry echo of her own S2 story, Eva going to the Heart as the bridge, and the closing narration with hey, sis. confidence high.
rows.per_story_synopsis: The finale keeps every promise the series made: Loroc's savior act collapses, Vanpa's magnet trap and the Fours sign-off buy the tunnel, and the creatures Eva once saved come back for her when the way is sealed. Rovender falls, asking only that she not let this change her, and it is Eight, finally given the jargum to hear Orbona speak, who breaks: the Heart greets her the way it once greeted Eva, with there is no them, only us, and the sister who ordered the war chooses re-entry, home, and love. Eva, the bridge, goes with the Heart, and the story ends in narration rather than battle, the world that was become the world that will be, past forgiven, future found, because there is no them, only us.
